posts.title: Why 45 Centimetres
posts.excerpt: An engineering dispatch from our Rotterdam workshop on counter clearances, wash rack sizing, and why forty-five centimetres preserves the workflow of small ten-seat kitchens.
posts.content:
In 2023, when Ines Aalders and Tomás Reyes founded Susugi Wash B.V. at our workshop on Werfstraat 12 in Rotterdam, the design brief started with a single physical measurement. Having worked behind a ten-seat dining counter, they knew that compact culinary spaces do not suffer from a lack of culinary ambition; they suffer from standard commercial dimensions. Conventional commercial dishwashers are built around the standard sixty-centimetre module or larger hood mechanisms designed for cavernous wash sculleries. In a dining room of ten to twelve seats, losing sixty centimetres of undercounter clearance often forces an operator to sacrifice essential refrigerated drawers, cutlery storage, or prep space.

The decision to engineer the Susugi Wash 45 around an overall width of 448 mm was therefore not an arbitrary styling choice, but a functional imperative. At 448 mm wide, 560 mm deep, and 820 mm high, the machine slides directly into the spatial void typically left by a narrow modular cabinet or a domestic undercounter footprint. Crucially, the 820 mm chassis height allows the unit to slide under counters with a finished clearance of 830 mm, aligning flush with adjacent stainless steel tabling without awkward elevation changes or custom joinery.

Downsizing an undercounter machine to forty-five centimetres presents immediate hydraulic and spatial challenges, particularly regarding the wash rack. Standard commercial dishwashers rely on 500 by 500 mm square baskets. For the Susugi Wash 45, the team developed a custom 400 by 400 mm rack format. This basket holds twenty-five glasses per wash cycle or dinner plates up to thirty centimetres in diameter. In practical service, twenty-five glasses represent the exact beverage turnover of two turns across a ten-seat counter. Running a ninety-second wash cycle means stemware can be cleared, washed, sanitised at 82 degrees Celsius, and returned to the station in less time than it takes to pour the next bottle.

Internal volume constraints also forced a total reconsideration of internal utilities. In a cramped kitchen, there is simply no floor space for secondary chemical booster boxes, external water softener cylinders, or floor-mounted drain pits. The Susugi Wash 45 integrates both an automated commercial drain pump and a built-in water softener within its compact 448 mm frame. Operating on a standard single-phase 230 V 16 A connection and consuming 2.4 litres of water per standard cycle, the machine operates independently of heavy commercial infrastructure.

Acoustic performance was the final non-negotiable factor during early testing. In a ten-seat restaurant, guests frequently sit within arm's reach of the pass. A loud wash pump or clattering door destroys dining room ambience instantly. By encasing the wash pump in targeted acoustic insulation, operational sound levels were brought down to 52 dB(A). Combined with a counterbalanced knee-height door fitted with a soft-closing friction hinge, the closing routine becomes calm and unobtrusive. For kitchens that need greater volume, the Susugi Wash 60 at 598 mm remains available, but forty-five centimetres remains the fundamental dimension that makes undercounter dishwashing viable in ten-seat dining rooms.

With preorders now open for our inaugural batch of 400 machines shipping from March 2027, every reservation backed by a refundable €200 deposit represents an endorsement of thoughtful spatial planning. Kitchens deserve equipment scaled precisely to their daily rhythm.
